reason: The cited evidence discusses limited atomic mobility in solid-state synthesis (E1, E2) and disorder-to-order transitions in HEA nanoparticles (E4), but none provides direct support for localized nanoscale melting, surface-energy-driven melting-point depression, or the role of transient liquid domains in governing the phase transition. The key premises about melting mechanisms are therefore largely unsupported by the referenced passages.
premises: High surface-to-volume ratio and defects lower the effective melting point locally in small HEA nanoparticles
Limited atomic mobility in the solid leads to an abrupt transition once nanoscale liquid domains form
Transient local liquid formation destabilizes the original solid solution and promotes atomic re-arrangement
Sluggish diffusion inherent to multi-element mixing further influences the phase transition process
Heating rate variations will measurably affect the onset and extent of the phase transition
